script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 14. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
A mistake is a gap between what you expected and what happened.  That gap is pure information—showing where your understanding was wrong.  Mistakes aren't failures; they're data.

When things work, you don't know why. Success confirms but doesn't explain. Failure demands explanation—forcing you to understand. Mistakes make you smarter in ways success can't. Mistakes only teach if you study them.  Quick shame and moving on wastes the lesson.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Errors are teachers, not enemies.  Mistakes reveal what success hides.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Mistake Analysis - What Did Failure Teach?.

Here's your activity: Think of a recent mistake or failure. What gap did it reveal between your expectations and reality? What specific lesson can you extract? How will you apply that learning going forward? This helps you extract lessons from recent mistakes.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about learning from getting it wrong can be applied to mistake analysis - what did failure teach?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
